extracted.intended_audience: new Flipboard users who want to create and manage Flipboard Magazines
extracted.subtask_description: Step‑by‑step guidance for creating, configuring, populating, and sharing a Flipboard Magazine on mobile or desktop. Covers naming, descriptions, tags, contributors, visibility, adding content, and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a Flipboard profile first
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you create your Flipboard profile, you’re just moments away from being able to create your first Flipboard Magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must have a profile before creating a magazine; on mobile or desktop start by selecting 'make a magazine' or clicking the + icon, then if prompted select 'for collecting.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Give the magazine a unique, indicative name
rubrics_metrics.description: Help your magazine stand out from all the others by giving it a unique name that still indicates what kind of stories readers will find inside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a name that signals content to readers so the magazine is noticeable and discoverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a clear and concise description
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear and concise description lets your readers know what kinds of content they can expect in the magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the description to set expectations and attract the right audience; keep it short and specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer multiple niche magazines to one broad topic
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend making multiple niche magazines instead of one with a broad topic. They are more fun to curate and make it easier for anyone to find useful and relevant information when browsing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create focused magazines for specific interests to improve curator enjoyment and reader relevance/discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add tags so content can appear in topic feeds
rubrics_metrics.description: Flipboard will tag content so that the stories you flip are eligible to appear in a relevant topic feed. If you’re creating your magazine on a desktop, you can add your own tags when you create the name and description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On desktop, manually add tags during magazine creation; rely on Flipboard’s tagging to make flipped stories show up in relevant topic feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite and manage contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: A Flipboard Magazine can be a collaborative effort between you and anyone you invite to participate. While you’re creating a magazine, you’ll be prompted to invite contributors, which you can do by sharing the magazine link via Facebook, email, text, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no limit to contributors. Only the magazine’s creator has admin rights and only the creator can delete items added by others. You can invite contributors later from the edit screen (desktop) or via the magazine’s settings on mobile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose magazine visibility: public or private
rubrics_metrics.description: You have the option to make your Flipboard Magazines public or private. A public magazine is just that—visible to anyone—but a private magazine can only be read by yourself and any contributors you’ve invited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You’re prompted to choose visibility when creating the magazine, but you can change it later from the edit screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add content from web, device, or within Flipboard
rubrics_metrics.description: You can add items from the Web, from your phone or tablet, or from within Flipboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the Web use the Flipboard Chrome Extension or bookmarklet and click the Flip It button in the toolbar. From phone/tablet use the device’s sharing function and select Flipboard (you’ll be prompted to pick a magazine). From within Flipboard click the + on any story you want to add.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share magazines to grow readership and start conversations
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you’ve created your Flipboard Magazine and added stories to it, you can use the share function to share it to your friends, family, or followers on social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing is an effective way to get more readers and to start a conversation with people who love the same things you do.
